questions.text: Who was the king of the Greek gods?

feedback: Poseidon was god of the sea
Hades ruled the Underworld
Apollo was god of music, healing and prophecy

questions.solution: Zeus ruled the gods from Mount Olympus and threw thunderbolts
questions.hint: He carried a thunderbolt

questions.text: Which Greek god ruled the sea and carried a trident? Give the Greek name.

feedback.Neptune: Neptune is his Roman name — give the Greek one

questions.solution: Poseidon was the Greek god of the sea, earthquakes and horses
questions.hint: He was a brother of Zeus

questions.text: What was the name of the three-headed dog that guarded the entrance to the Underworld?

feedback: Charon was the ferryman of the dead
The Minotaur was half man, half bull
Pegasus was a winged horse

questions.solution: Cerberus guarded the gates of the Underworld so the dead could not leave
questions.hint: Heracles had to capture it in his final labour

questions.text: Twin brothers were said to have been raised by a she-wolf, and one of them founded Rome. Give the name of the founder.

feedback.Remus: Remus was the twin; Rome is named after his brother

questions.solution: Romulus was said to have founded Rome, which was named after him
questions.hint: The city's name comes from his name

questions.text: Which Greek hero carried out twelve labours?

feedback: Theseus is famous for killing the Minotaur
Perseus is famous for killing Medusa
Jason is famous for the Golden Fleece

questions.solution: Heracles carried out twelve labours for King Eurystheus
questions.hint: His first labour was to kill the Nemean lion

questions.text: Who ferried the souls of the dead across the river into the Underworld? Give the name.

feedback.Chiron: Chiron was the wise centaur who taught heroes; the ferryman has a different name

questions.solution: Charon ferried the dead across the river into the Underworld
questions.hint: The dead were buried with a coin to pay him

questions.text: What is the Roman name for the Greek goddess Athena?

feedback: Venus is the Roman name for Aphrodite
Diana is the Roman name for Artemis
Juno is the Roman name for Hera

questions.solution: The Romans identified Athena with Minerva, goddess of wisdom and crafts
questions.hint: She was goddess of wisdom

questions.text: What was a libation?

options: Pouring a liquid, such as wine, as an offering to a god
Killing an animal at an altar
A building that held a god's statue
A priest who read the flight of birds
feedback: That is an animal sacrifice
That is a temple
That is an augur

questions.solution: A libation was a liquid offering, often wine, poured out for a god
questions.hint: Think about drink rather than food

questions.text: Which monster did Theseus kill in the Labyrinth on Crete?

feedback: Heracles killed the Hydra
Perseus killed Medusa
Heracles killed the Nemean lion

questions.solution: Theseus killed the Minotaur, half man and half bull, in the Labyrinth
questions.hint: It was half man and half bull

questions.text: Which princess of Crete gave Theseus a ball of thread to find his way out of the Labyrinth? Give the name.
questions.solution: Ariadne gave Theseus a thread so he could retrace his steps
questions.hint: She was the daughter of King Minos

questions.text: Which Trojan hero, son of Venus, escaped from Troy and became the ancestor of the Romans? Give the name.
questions.solution: Aeneas carried his father out of burning Troy and travelled to Italy
questions.hint: Virgil wrote an epic poem about him

questions.text: What was the main room of a Greek temple, which held the statue of the god, called?

feedback: The altar stood outside, in front of the temple, where sacrifices took place
A stoa was a covered walkway
The agora was the marketplace and meeting place

questions.solution: The cella (naos) was the inner room that housed the cult statue
questions.hint: Worship and sacrifice happened outside, so the statue was kept in an inner room

questions.text: A Roman family keeps a small shrine at home and offers food to its household spirits. What is the shrine called?

feedback: The forum was the main public square of a town
A basilica was a hall for law courts and business
The atrium was the main hall of a house, not a shrine

questions.solution: The lararium was the household shrine to the Lares, the spirits who protected the family
questions.hint: It is named after the household spirits, the Lares

questions.text: A Greek city wants to ask Apollo's oracle for advice before going to war. Where should its messengers go?

feedback: Olympia was the great sanctuary of Zeus, where the Games were held

questions.solution: Apollo's most famous oracle was at Delphi, where the Pythia gave his answers
questions.hint: The priestess there was called the Pythia

questions.text: How did Heracles clean the huge Augean stables in a single day?

options: He used a magic broom from Athena
He diverted two rivers through the stables
He paid local farmers to do the work

questions.solution: Heracles changed the course of two rivers so they washed the stables clean
questions.hint: He used the power of nature rather than his own hands

questions.text: Persephone spends part of every year in the Underworld. What does this myth explain?
questions.solution: While Persephone is below, her mother Demeter grieves and crops do not grow, giving winter
questions.hint: Think about what happens to crops when Demeter is sad

questions.text: Which Greek god was the messenger of the gods, wore winged sandals and guided souls to the Underworld? Give the Greek name.

feedback.Mercury: Mercury is his Roman name — give the Greek one

questions.solution: Hermes was the messenger god and guided the souls of the dead to the Underworld
questions.hint: He was also the god of travellers and thieves

questions.text: Which mountain was believed to be the home of the main Greek gods? Give the name.

feedback.Olympia: Olympia was the sanctuary of Zeus where the Games were held; the gods lived on a mountain

questions.solution: The twelve main gods were believed to live on Mount Olympus
questions.hint: The twelve main gods take their group name from it

questions.text: A Greek vase shows a hero wearing a lion skin and carrying a club. Which hero is it?
questions.solution: Heracles wore the skin of the Nemean lion and carried a club
questions.hint: Think about which hero killed a lion in his first labour

questions.text: A Roman priest inspects the liver of a sacrificed animal to learn the will of the gods. What was he called?

feedback: An augur read signs from the flight and behaviour of birds
The Vestal Virgins tended the sacred fire of Vesta
The Pontifex Maximus was the chief priest of Rome

questions.solution: A haruspex examined the entrails, especially the liver, of sacrificed animals
questions.hint: This practice came to Rome from the Etruscans

questions.text: Which pair shows a Greek god with the correct Roman name?

feedback: Hera's Roman name is Juno
Hephaestus's Roman name is Vulcan
Artemis's Roman name is Diana

questions.solution: Ares, the god of war, was identified with the Roman god Mars
questions.hint: Match the gods by their roles: war, marriage, the forge, hunting

questions.text: In the Roman foundation myth, Romulus and Remus were said to be sons of which god?
questions.solution: The twins were said to be sons of Mars and Rhea Silvia, a Vestal Virgin
questions.hint: He was the Roman god of war

questions.text: Which Greek goddess of the harvest searched for her daughter after the girl was taken to the Underworld? Give the Greek name.

feedback.Ceres: Ceres is her Roman name — give the Greek one

questions.solution: Demeter searched for her daughter Persephone, and the crops failed while she grieved
questions.hint: Her daughter was Persephone

questions.text: Describe two things that happened during a Greek animal sacrifice.

rubric.model_answer: Worshippers walked in a procession to the altar outside the temple, leading the animal, which was decorated with ribbons. They washed their hands in water to purify themselves, sprinkled barley grains and prayed to the god. The animal was then killed at the altar; the thigh bones wrapped in fat were burned for the god, and the meat was cooked and shared in a feast.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one stage (e.g. procession, purification, prayer)
1 mark: supporting detail
1 mark: identifies a second stage (e.g. offering burned, shared feast)
1 mark: supporting detail

questions.solution: A sacrifice involved a procession, purification and prayer, an offering at the altar and a shared feast
questions.hint: Think about what happened before, during and after the offering at the altar

questions.text: Why was the sacred fire of Vesta kept burning in Rome?

options: The fire was used to cook food for gladiators
The fire lit the Colosseum at night
The fire heated the public baths
Romans believed its flame protected the city

questions.solution: Romans believed that if Vesta's flame went out, disaster could fall on Rome
questions.hint: Vesta was the goddess of the hearth, the heart of the home and the city

questions.text: Which statement about Greek religion is accurate?

options: Greek religion had no single holy book and was based on rituals such as sacrifice
Greek religion was based on one holy book written by Homer
The Greeks worshipped only one god
Only priests were allowed to pray
feedback: Homer's poems were very important, but they were not a holy book of rules

questions.solution: Greek religion centred on rituals, festivals and sacrifice rather than a holy book
questions.hint: Think about the importance of altars and festivals

questions.text: Why did the Romans see Aeneas as a model of 'pietas'?

options: He did his duty to the gods, his family and his country

questions.solution: Aeneas carried his father and household gods from Troy and obeyed the gods' command to go to Italy
questions.hint: Pietas means duty

questions.text: Which statement about the Greek Underworld is accurate?

options: Everyone went to Mount Olympus after death
The Underworld was ruled by Zeus
Heroes and the virtuous might go to Elysium, and the wicked to Tartarus
The dead were reborn as gods
feedback: Hades ruled the Underworld; Zeus ruled from Olympus

questions.solution: The Underworld, ruled by Hades, included Elysium for the blessed and Tartarus for the wicked
questions.hint: Think about the different regions of the Underworld

questions.text: Why did the Athenians see Theseus as an especially important hero?

options: He won the Trojan War single-handed
He was the first Roman emperor
He was believed to have united Attica and freed Athens from sending young people to the Minotaur

questions.solution: Athenians honoured Theseus as their national hero, who united Attica and ended the tribute to Crete
questions.hint: Think about what Theseus did for his own city

questions.text: Explain two ways the Romans honoured their gods in everyday life.

rubric.model_answer: Roman families worshipped household gods, the Lares and Penates, at a lararium shrine at home, where the head of the family led prayers and offered small gifts such as food, wine or incense. Romans also took part in public religion: they attended festivals such as Saturnalia and watched sacrifices at temples, where priests offered animals on altars to keep the gods' favour.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one way (e.g. household worship)
1 mark: supporting detail
1 mark: identifies a second way (e.g. festivals, public sacrifice)
1 mark: supporting detail

questions.solution: Romans worshipped both at home and in public festivals and sacrifices
questions.hint: Think about worship at home and in the city

questions.text: In Homer's Odyssey, who was the faithful wife of Odysseus who waited 20 years for him to return? Give the name.
questions.solution: Penelope waited 20 years for Odysseus: ten years of war and ten years of his journey home
questions.hint: She lived on Ithaca with her son Telemachus

questions.text: Which goddess did the Vestal Virgins serve?

feedback: Venus was the goddess of love
Minerva was the goddess of wisdom
Juno was the queen of the gods

questions.solution: The Vestal Virgins served Vesta, goddess of the hearth, and kept her sacred fire burning
questions.hint: She was the goddess of the hearth

questions.text: Which Roman emperor was Livia's husband?
questions.solution: Livia was married to Augustus, the first Roman emperor, for over 50 years
questions.hint: He was the first Roman emperor

questions.text: What is the Latin term for the male head of a Roman family, who had legal power over his household? Give the term.
questions.solution: The paterfamilias had legal power (patria potestas) over his children and household
questions.hint: The first part of the term means father

questions.text: In which Greek city-state did girls take part in public athletics and exercise?

feedback: Athenian girls mostly stayed at home learning household skills

questions.solution: Spartan girls ran, wrestled and threw the javelin, because Spartans believed fit mothers had strong children
questions.hint: This city-state was famous for its soldiers

questions.text: What is the Greek term for the male guardian who was legally responsible for an Athenian woman? Give the term.
questions.solution: A woman's kyrios, usually her father and later her husband, acted for her in legal matters
questions.hint: It was usually her father, and later her husband

questions.text: How did Penelope delay choosing a new husband from the suitors?

options: She locked herself in a tower
She set the suitors a chariot race
She wove a shroud by day and unpicked it at night

questions.solution: Penelope said she would choose once a burial shroud for Laertes was finished, then secretly undid it each night
questions.hint: Think about weaving, the work of a Greek household

questions.text: How long did a Vestal Virgin usually serve as a priestess?

options: Her whole life, with no choice to leave
feedback: After 30 years a Vestal could leave and marry if she wished

questions.solution: Vestals served for 30 years: 10 learning, 10 performing the rites and 10 teaching
questions.hint: Their service was split into three equal stages of ten years

questions.text: Which statement about Spartan women, compared with Athenian women, is accurate?

options: Spartan women were not allowed outside the house
Spartan women could own and manage land
Spartan women could vote in the assembly

questions.solution: Spartan women could own land and ran estates while men were away training or at war
questions.hint: Think about who looked after the land while Spartan men were soldiers

questions.text: What was the long dress worn by respectable married Roman women called? Give the Latin term.

feedback.toga: The toga was worn by male Roman citizens

questions.solution: A married Roman woman wore a stola over her tunic as a sign of respectability
questions.hint: Men wore the toga; married women wore this instead

questions.text: In both Athens and Rome, what was the money or property a bride's family gave when she married called? Give the term.
questions.solution: The dowry was given with the bride and usually had to be returned if the marriage ended
questions.hint: It usually had to be returned if the marriage ended

questions.text: What were the women's quarters in an Athenian house called?

feedback: The andron was the men's dining room, used for symposia
The agora was the public marketplace
A stoa was a covered walkway

questions.solution: Athenian women spent much of their time in the gynaikon, often at the back or upstairs
questions.hint: The word starts with the Greek for woman, as in 'gynaecology'

questions.text: Athenian women take part in a festival for Demeter from which men are excluded. Which festival is this?

feedback: The Panathenaia honoured Athena and men took part
Saturnalia was a Roman festival

questions.solution: The Thesmophoria was a women-only festival for Demeter, linked to fertility and the harvest
questions.hint: Demeter was goddess of the harvest; think about a festival for women only

questions.text: Roman daughters were usually named after their father's family name. What would a daughter of the Cornelius family be called?

feedback: Cornelius is the male form of the name

questions.solution: Daughters took the feminine form of the family name, so a Cornelius's daughter was Cornelia
questions.hint: Change the ending to a feminine one

questions.text: A Spartan mother tells her son to come back from battle 'with your shield or on it'. What does this show about Spartan values?

options: Spartans did not care about their children
Courage in battle mattered more than personal safety
Shields were very expensive in Sparta

questions.solution: The saying shows that Spartans valued courage: dropping your shield to run away was shameful
questions.hint: Think about what a soldier who ran away would leave behind

questions.text: A wealthy Roman widow manages her family's property and hosts dinner parties for her late husband's clients. Which statement does this support?

options: Roman women were never allowed to leave the house
Roman women could vote in elections
Some wealthy Roman women had real influence and independence

questions.solution: Wealthy Roman women could own property, attend dinners and act as patrons
questions.hint: Look for the statement that matches what the widow is actually doing

questions.text: Which wife of the emperor Augustus was given the title 'Augusta' after his death? Give her name.
questions.solution: After Augustus died in AD 14, Livia was adopted into his family and given the title Augusta
questions.hint: She was the mother of the emperor Tiberius

questions.text: Which Spartan princess was the first woman to win at the Olympic Games, as owner of a winning chariot team? Give her name.
questions.solution: Cynisca of Sparta won the four-horse chariot race as owner of the team
questions.hint: She was the sister of the Spartan king Agesilaus

questions.text: A Roman woman's tombstone praises her because 'she kept the house and worked wool'. What does this suggest Romans valued in a woman?

options: Modesty and skill in running the household

questions.solution: Epitaphs like this praise traditional virtues: running the home and spinning wool
questions.hint: Think about where the woman spent her time

questions.text: Which statement correctly compares girls in Athens and Sparta?

options: Spartan girls had physical training; Athenian girls mostly learned household skills at home
Athenian girls trained as soldiers; Spartan girls stayed at home
Both went to public schools with boys

questions.solution: Spartan girls exercised in public, while Athenian girls learned spinning, weaving and running a home
questions.hint: Think about which city valued physical fitness for girls

questions.text: Which privileges did the Vestal Virgins have that most Roman women did not?

options: They were free from their father's legal power and had special seats at public shows

questions.solution: Vestals were freed from patria potestas, could make a will and had seats of honour at the games
questions.hint: Think about their legal status and their place at public events

questions.text: In the Odyssey, how does Penelope test whether the stranger really is Odysseus?

options: She asks him to kill a sea monster
She asks him to name all the suitors
She asks for their bed to be moved, which only Odysseus knows is impossible
She asks him to weave a shroud

questions.solution: Only Odysseus knew the bed was built around a living olive tree, so it could not be moved
questions.hint: Think about a secret only husband and wife would share

questions.text: Which queen of the Iceni led a revolt against Roman rule in Britain? Give her name.
questions.solution: Boudica, queen of the Iceni, led a major revolt against the Romans in Britain in about AD 60
questions.hint: Her tribe lived in what is now East Anglia

questions.text: Describe two ways the lives of Spartan women were different from those of Athenian women.

rubric.model_answer: Spartan girls exercised in public, running and wrestling, because Spartans believed fit mothers had strong children; Athenian girls stayed mostly at home learning to spin and weave. Spartan women could own and run land and managed estates while men served in the army, whereas Athenian women needed a male guardian (kyrios) for legal and property matters. Spartan women also married later than Athenian girls.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one difference (e.g. physical training)
1 mark: supporting detail
1 mark: identifies a second difference (e.g. owning land, age of marriage)
1 mark: supporting detail

questions.solution: Spartan women had more physical freedom and control of property than Athenian women
questions.hint: Think about exercise, property and marriage

questions.text: Which statement about the evidence for Athenian women's lives is accurate?

options: Many diaries written by Athenian women survive
Athenian women wrote most of the city's laws
There is no evidence at all about them
Most surviving written sources were written by men

questions.solution: Most written evidence about Athenian women comes from men, so historians use it with care
questions.hint: Think about who wrote the plays, speeches and histories that survive

questions.text: Why might Penelope be seen as an ideal wife in the Odyssey?

options: She stayed loyal to Odysseus and protected his household for 20 years
She quickly married one of the suitors
She left Ithaca to fight at Troy
She ruled Troy after the war

questions.solution: Penelope's loyalty and cleverness protected Odysseus' home and son until he returned
questions.hint: Think about how she dealt with the suitors

questions.text: Why was Livia able to be so influential in Rome?

options: She was close to Augustus and was the mother of the next emperor, Tiberius
She was the chief Vestal Virgin

questions.solution: Livia advised Augustus and her son Tiberius became emperor, so she had great informal power
questions.hint: Think about her husband and her son

questions.text: Which statement about Roman women and the law is accurate?

options: Women could stand for election as consuls
Women were legally equal to men in every way
Women could not vote or hold political office
Women could vote in the Senate

questions.solution: Roman women had no vote and could not be magistrates, though some had influence through their families
questions.hint: Think about who could take part in Roman elections

questions.text: Why did the Romans treat the Vestal Virgins with such respect?

options: The Vestals were the richest people in Rome
The Vestals were all daughters of the emperor
The Vestals ran the public baths
They believed the Vestals kept the city safe by tending the sacred flame of Vesta

questions.solution: Romans believed Rome's safety depended on the Vestals keeping Vesta's fire alight and performing the rites correctly
questions.hint: Think about what the Vestals looked after

questions.text: Explain two ways women could have influence in ancient Athens or Rome, even though they could not vote.

rubric.model_answer: Women held important religious roles: in Athens the priestess of Athena Polias and women at festivals such as the Thesmophoria, and in Rome the Vestal Virgins, were respected and believed to protect the city. Wealthy women could also influence politics through their families: Livia advised her husband Augustus and helped her son Tiberius become emperor, and Roman women could manage property and act as patrons.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one way (e.g. religious roles)
1 mark: supporting example
1 mark: identifies a second way (e.g. family influence, property)
1 mark: supporting example

questions.solution: Women gained influence through religion and through their families and wealth
questions.hint: Think about religious roles and powerful families

questions.text: Who is the hero of Homer's Odyssey?

feedback: Achilles is the hero of the Iliad
Hector is the Trojan prince in the Iliad
Aeneas is the hero of Virgil's Aeneid

questions.solution: The Odyssey tells of Odysseus' ten-year journey home from Troy
questions.hint: The poem is named after him

questions.text: What is the Greek word for the custom of hospitality between guests and hosts? Give the term.
questions.solution: Xenia (guest-friendship) required hosts to welcome strangers and guests to respect their hosts
questions.hint: Zeus was believed to protect this custom

questions.text: Which Trojan prince does Achilles kill in the Iliad?

feedback: Paris survives the Iliad; later stories say he shot Achilles
Priam is the old king who later asks for his son's body
Aeneas survives the war and escapes from Troy

questions.solution: Achilles kills Hector to avenge the death of Patroclus
questions.hint: He was the eldest son of King Priam

questions.text: Which island was Odysseus king of? Give the name.
questions.solution: Odysseus was king of Ithaca, an island off the west coast of Greece
questions.hint: It is an island off the west coast of Greece

questions.text: What was the name of the one-eyed giant whom Odysseus blinded?

feedback: Cerberus guarded the Underworld
Charybdis was a whirlpool monster

questions.solution: Polyphemus was a Cyclops and a son of Poseidon
questions.hint: He was a Cyclops and a son of Poseidon

questions.text: Which king of Mycenae led the Greek army at Troy? Give the name.
questions.solution: Agamemnon, king of Mycenae, was the commander of the Greek army
questions.hint: His brother was Menelaus, Helen's husband

questions.text: Why does Achilles refuse to fight at the start of the Iliad?

options: Zeus has told him the war is over
He has been wounded in the heel
Agamemnon has taken away his prize, Briseis
feedback: The story of the heel comes from later legends, not the Iliad

questions.solution: Agamemnon takes Briseis from Achilles, insulting his honour, so Achilles withdraws from the fighting
questions.hint: It is a quarrel about honour between two Greek leaders

questions.text: What does 'kleos' mean in the Homeric world?

options: Glory or fame that lives on after death
feedback: Hospitality is xenia
The journey home is nostos

questions.solution: Heroes fought for kleos, the glory that would make their names remembered
questions.hint: Achilles chose a short life with this rather than a long, quiet one

questions.text: What did Odysseus tell the Cyclops his name was?
questions.solution: Odysseus said his name was 'Nobody', so when the Cyclops shouted that Nobody was hurting him, no one came
questions.hint: Think about what the other Cyclopes heard when Polyphemus called for aid

questions.text: Who was Odysseus' son, who searched for news of his father? Give the name.
questions.solution: Telemachus travels to Pylos and Sparta for news of Odysseus, then helps him defeat the suitors
questions.hint: He was a baby when his father left for Troy

questions.text: Which Greek warrior, Achilles' close companion, was killed by Hector while wearing Achilles' armour? Give the name.
questions.solution: Patroclus' death made Achilles return to battle
questions.hint: His death made Achilles return to the fighting

questions.text: What is 'nostos', an important theme in the Odyssey?

feedback: Guest-friendship is xenia

questions.solution: Nostos means homecoming, the theme of Odysseus' journey back to Ithaca
questions.hint: The word is linked to 'nostalgia', a longing for home

questions.text: In the Odyssey, the suitors eat Odysseus' food for years without his permission. Which Homeric value are they breaking?

feedback: Kleos is glory or fame
Nostos is the homecoming
Aristeia is a warrior's moment of glory in battle

questions.solution: The suitors misuse their position as guests, breaking the rules of xenia
questions.hint: Think about the rules for guests and hosts

questions.text: Homer describes 'swift-footed Achilles' and 'grey-eyed Athena'. What are these descriptions called?

feedback: A simile compares one thing to another using 'like' or 'as'

questions.solution: Epithets are fixed descriptive phrases that helped bards compose and remember the poems
questions.hint: They are repeated whenever the character is named

questions.text: In the Odyssey, how does Odysseus escape from the Cyclops' cave?

options: By clinging to the underside of the sheep
By swimming through an underground river
By hiding inside a wooden horse

questions.solution: Odysseus and his men held on under the sheep as the blinded Cyclops let them out to graze
questions.hint: The Cyclops felt the animals' backs as they left the cave

questions.text: Odysseus has wax put in his crew's ears and is tied to the mast. Which danger is he facing?
questions.solution: The Sirens' song lured sailors to their deaths, so Odysseus' crew blocked their ears
questions.hint: This danger could only be heard, not seen

questions.text: Which archaeologist excavated at Troy (Hisarlik) and Mycenae in the 1870s? Give the surname.
questions.solution: Heinrich Schliemann dug at Hisarlik from 1870 and at Mycenae in 1876
questions.hint: He was a wealthy German businessman

questions.text: What is the great gateway into the citadel of Mycenae, carved with two large animals, called? Give the name.
questions.solution: The Lion Gate was the main entrance to the citadel of Mycenae
questions.hint: The animals are big cats

questions.text: In the last book of the Iliad, King Priam goes to Achilles' hut. Why?

options: To challenge Achilles to a duel
To give Helen back to the Greeks
To ask for the body of his son Hector

questions.solution: Priam begs Achilles to return Hector's body, and Achilles, moved to pity, agrees
questions.hint: Think about what Achilles had done after killing Hector

questions.text: Odysseus returns home disguised as a beggar. Who recognises him from a scar while washing his feet?

feedback: Penelope recognises him later, with the test of the bed
Argos recognises Odysseus, but not from a scar

questions.solution: Eurycleia recognises the scar on his leg from a boar hunt in his youth
questions.hint: She had looked after him when he was a baby

questions.text: Which of these is NOT an event in the Iliad?

options: The Greeks enter Troy in the Wooden Horse
Priam visits Achilles to ask for Hector's body

questions.solution: The Iliad ends with Hector's funeral; the Wooden Horse is described in the Odyssey and the Aeneid
questions.hint: Think about how the Iliad ends

questions.text: What was Linear B?

options: An early form of Greek writing on clay tablets from Mycenaean palaces

questions.solution: Linear B tablets, deciphered in 1952, record the palace accounts of Mycenaean Greece
questions.hint: Michael Ventris deciphered it in 1952

questions.text: Which loyal swineherd gives shelter to Odysseus when he returns to Ithaca disguised as a beggar? Give the name.
questions.solution: Eumaeus the swineherd welcomes the 'beggar' kindly, showing good xenia
questions.hint: He looks after Odysseus' pigs

questions.text: Describe two examples of xenia, good or bad, in the Odyssey.

rubric.model_answer: Good xenia is shown by the Phaeacians: King Alcinous and Queen Arete welcome Odysseus, feed him, give him gifts and promise him a ship home before they even know his name. Bad xenia is shown by the Cyclops Polyphemus, who traps Odysseus and his men in his cave and attacks them instead of welcoming them, and by the suitors, who eat Odysseus' food and insult him when he is disguised as a beggar.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one example (e.g. the Phaeacians)
1 mark: explains how it shows good or bad xenia
1 mark: identifies a second example (e.g. Polyphemus, the suitors, Eumaeus)
1 mark: explains how it shows good or bad xenia

questions.solution: The Phaeacians and Eumaeus show good xenia; Polyphemus and the suitors break it
questions.hint: Think about how Odysseus is treated as a guest in different places

questions.text: Why is Hector often seen as a sympathetic hero in the Iliad?

options: He refuses to fight for most of the poem
He breaks the rules of xenia
He fights to protect his city and family, knowing he may die

questions.solution: Hector defends Troy out of duty, and his farewell to Andromache and his son shows his love for his family
questions.hint: Think about his farewell to his wife and baby son

questions.text: Which statement about the Homeric poems is accurate?

options: They come from an oral tradition and were performed by bards
They were written in Latin by Virgil
They were first written as prose novels
They describe the founding of Rome
feedback: Virgil wrote the Aeneid in Latin, centuries later

questions.solution: The Iliad and Odyssey grew from oral poetry performed by bards, which is why they use epithets and repetition
questions.hint: Think about the bard Demodocus in the Odyssey

questions.text: Why does Poseidon make Odysseus' journey home so difficult?

options: Odysseus blinded his son, the Cyclops Polyphemus
Odysseus refused to fight at Troy

questions.solution: Polyphemus prayed to his father Poseidon for revenge after Odysseus blinded him
questions.hint: Think about who Polyphemus' father was

questions.text: Which statement about Schliemann's finds at Mycenae is accurate?

options: He proved the Iliad is entirely true
He found Odysseus' palace on Ithaca
The gold 'Mask of Agamemnon' is now thought to be older than the time of the Trojan War
He showed that Linear B was a form of Latin

questions.solution: The mask is dated to about 1550–1500 BC, around 300 years before the traditional date of the Trojan War
questions.hint: Think about whether the mask could really have belonged to Agamemnon

questions.text: How does the death of Patroclus change the course of the Iliad?

options: It makes Achilles return to battle to take revenge on Hector

questions.solution: Grief and anger at Patroclus' death bring Achilles back into the war, leading to Hector's death
questions.hint: Think about how Achilles reacts to losing his closest friend

questions.text: Explain two ways Achilles shows the values of a Homeric hero in the Iliad.

rubric.model_answer: Achilles is the greatest warrior at Troy and seeks kleos, lasting glory: he chooses a short, glorious life over a long, quiet one. He also cares greatly about timē, his honour: when Agamemnon takes his prize Briseis, he withdraws from battle because his honour has been insulted. After Patroclus dies he returns and kills Hector, and in the last book he shows pity by returning Hector's body to Priam.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one value (e.g. kleos)
1 mark: supports it with an event
1 mark: identifies a second value (e.g. honour, loyalty to friends)
1 mark: supports it with an event

questions.solution: Achilles shows the hero's search for glory and his concern for honour
questions.hint: Think about kleos and honour

questions.text: In which year AD did Vesuvius erupt and bury Pompeii? Give the year.
questions.solution: Vesuvius erupted in AD 79 and buried Pompeii and Herculaneum
questions.hint: It happened in the first year of the emperor Titus's reign

questions.text: What was a Roman insula?

options: A large house for one wealthy family
feedback: A large family house was a domus

questions.solution: Most people in Rome lived in insulae, blocks of flats several storeys high
questions.hint: The word means island, because the block stood alone surrounded by streets

questions.text: Where did people in Rome watch chariot races?

feedback: The Colosseum was used for gladiator fights and beast hunts
The Forum was the main public square
The Pantheon was a temple

questions.solution: Chariot races took place in the Circus Maximus, a long track for huge crowds
questions.hint: It was a long racetrack, not a round arena

questions.text: What was the hot room in a Roman bath house called? Give the Latin term.

feedback.frigidarium: The frigidarium was the cold room
feedback.tepidarium: The tepidarium was the warm room

questions.solution: The caldarium was the hot room, heated by the hypocaust
questions.hint: Bathers usually reached it after the warm room

questions.text: What was the forum in a Roman town?

options: The main public square, used for business, politics and religion

questions.solution: The forum was the centre of public life, surrounded by temples, the basilica and offices
questions.hint: Think about the centre of town life

questions.text: What is the Latin word for a large Roman town house belonging to a wealthy family? Give the term.

feedback.insula: An insula was a block of flats

questions.solution: A domus was a private town house, built around an atrium
questions.hint: English words such as 'domestic' come from it

questions.text: What was the impluvium in a Roman house?

options: A shallow pool in the atrium that collected rainwater
feedback: The dining room was the triclinium
The kitchen was the culina
A bedroom was a cubiculum

questions.solution: Rain fell through the compluvium (an opening in the roof) into the impluvium below
questions.hint: It sat under an opening in the roof

questions.text: Which type of gladiator fought with a net and a trident?

feedback: A murmillo had a sword, a large shield and a helmet with a fish crest
The secutor had a smooth, round helmet and often fought the net-fighter
A Thraex (Thracian) fought with a small shield and a curved sword

questions.solution: The retiarius fought with a net, a trident and a dagger, with little armour
questions.hint: His name comes from the Latin word for net

questions.text: What was the triclinium?

options: The cold room at the baths
The dining room, where diners reclined on couches
feedback: The cold room was the frigidarium
The entrance hall was the atrium
The colonnaded garden was the peristylium

questions.solution: The triclinium had three couches where diners reclined to eat
questions.hint: Its name refers to three couches

questions.text: What was the morning visit made by clients to their patron's house called? Give the Latin term.
questions.solution: At the salutatio clients greeted their patron in his atrium and asked for help or gifts
questions.hint: It comes from the Latin verb meaning to greet

questions.text: In which room of a Roman house was the compluvium, an opening in the roof? Give the Latin name of the room.
questions.solution: The atrium was the main hall near the entrance, with the compluvium above and the impluvium below
questions.hint: It was the main hall just inside the entrance

questions.text: Which of these was one of the four chariot-racing teams (factions) in Rome?
questions.solution: The four factions were the Reds, Whites, Blues and Greens
questions.hint: The teams were named after colours: red, white, blue and one more

questions.text: At the baths, a Roman wants to scrape oil and sweat off his skin. Which tool does he use?

feedback: A stylus was used for writing on wax tablets
A trident was a gladiator's weapon
A rudis was the wooden sword given to a freed gladiator

questions.solution: Romans rubbed oil on their skin and scraped it off with a curved metal strigil
questions.hint: Romans did not use soap, so they needed a scraper

questions.text: A wealthy Roman pays for gladiator games in his town just before an election. What is this an example of?

options: Using public entertainment to win political support

questions.solution: Wealthy Romans paid for games to win popularity and votes
questions.hint: Think about why he chose the time just before an election

questions.text: A client goes with his patron to the forum and votes for him. What would the client usually receive in return?

options: Gifts of food or money (the sportula) and legal support

questions.solution: Patrons gave clients the sportula (a gift of food or money) and helped them, for example in court
questions.hint: The relationship worked both ways

questions.text: Archaeologists in Pompeii find a counter facing the street with large jars set into it. What kind of business was this?
questions.solution: A thermopolium sold hot food and drink from jars (dolia) set into a street counter
questions.hint: Think about street food

questions.text: What was the Roman underfloor heating system used in baths called? Give the term.
questions.solution: In a hypocaust hot air from a furnace flowed under floors raised on stacks of tiles
questions.hint: Hot air from a furnace flowed under floors raised on stacks of tiles

questions.text: What is the large amphitheatre in Rome, opened in AD 80, usually called today? Give the name.
questions.solution: The Colosseum (Flavian Amphitheatre) opened in AD 80 under the emperor Titus
questions.hint: Its name may come from a giant statue of Nero that stood nearby

questions.text: Pliny the Younger wrote two letters describing a huge dark cloud, falling ash and his uncle's rescue voyage. Which event was he describing?

options: The Great Fire of Rome in AD 64
The eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79

questions.solution: Pliny's letters to the historian Tacitus are eyewitness accounts of the eruption of Vesuvius
questions.hint: Think about where falling ash would come from

questions.text: Which statement about life in an insula is accurate?

options: Upper floors were often cheaper but at greater risk from fire
Every flat had its own running water and toilet
feedback: The ground floors of insulae often had shops (tabernae)

questions.solution: The poorest tenants rented cramped upper floors, which were hardest to escape in a fire; the ground floor often had shops
questions.hint: Think about carrying water upstairs and escaping a fire

questions.text: A wall painting from Pompeii shows a riot in the amphitheatre. Tacitus says that in AD 59 people from Pompeii and Nuceria fought there. What did the Senate do?

options: Banned such shows in Pompeii for ten years

questions.solution: The Senate banned gatherings like this in Pompeii for ten years, according to Tacitus
questions.hint: Think about how the authorities would punish a town for a riot

questions.text: Which pair correctly matches a room in a domus with its use?

options: Tablinum – the master's study or office
feedback: The culina was the kitchen
The peristylium was the colonnaded garden
A cubiculum was a bedroom

questions.solution: The tablinum was the master's study between the atrium and the peristyle garden
questions.hint: Rule out the ones you know are wrong first

questions.text: What was the wooden sword given to a gladiator when he was granted his freedom called? Give the Latin term.
questions.solution: A freed gladiator received a rudis, a wooden sword, as a symbol that he would not have to fight again
questions.hint: It was given as a symbol that he would not have to fight again

questions.text: Describe two features of a wealthy Roman domus.

rubric.model_answer: The atrium was the main hall near the entrance, with an opening in the roof (compluvium) above a pool (impluvium) that collected rainwater; clients waited here during the salutatio. At the back, many houses had a peristylium, a garden surrounded by columns. The triclinium was the dining room where guests reclined on couches, and walls and floors were often decorated with paintings and mosaics.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one feature (e.g. atrium)
1 mark: describes its appearance or use
1 mark: identifies a second feature (e.g. peristylium, triclinium, mosaics)
1 mark: describes its appearance or use

questions.solution: The atrium, peristylium, triclinium and decoration are key features of a domus
questions.hint: Think about walking in from the street to the back of the house

questions.text: Why are Pompeii and Herculaneum such important sources for Roman city life?

options: They were capital cities of the empire
They were never damaged by the eruption
They were built after the eruption
The eruption preserved buildings, objects and graffiti as they were in AD 79

questions.solution: Buried by the eruption, the towns preserve houses, shops, paintings and graffiti from AD 79
questions.hint: Think about what the volcanic ash did to the towns

questions.text: Why did wealthy Romans pay for public buildings and games?

options: To gain prestige and political support from citizens
The law made every citizen build a temple
To avoid paying for their own houses
Only enslaved people could attend the games

questions.solution: Paying for buildings and games showed generosity and won popularity and votes
questions.hint: Think about what a politician gains from public generosity

questions.text: Which statement about the patron and client system is accurate?

options: Clients were enslaved people owned by the patron
Patrons and clients had duties to each other: a richer patron helped less powerful clients
Patrons had to obey their clients
The system was banned in Rome
feedback: Clients were free people, often including freedmen

questions.solution: Patrons protected and helped their clients, who gave them support, votes and respect in return
questions.hint: Think about what each side gave the other

questions.text: Which statement about Roman baths is accurate?

options: Only the emperor could use them
They were only open at night
They were social places where people met, exercised and did business as well as washed

questions.solution: Baths were social centres with exercise yards, snack sellers and meeting places
questions.hint: Think about what else people did at the baths besides washing

questions.text: Why might a gladiator who fought bravely be allowed to live even after losing?

options: Losers were always given their freedom
The Senate voted on every fight
The crowd and the sponsor of the games could grant him missio (release)

questions.solution: The editor (sponsor), often guided by the crowd, could spare a defeated gladiator who had fought well
questions.hint: Think about who decided the result of a fight

questions.text: Explain two reasons why gladiator games were popular in Roman towns.

rubric.model_answer: They were exciting public entertainment, free for spectators and paid for by wealthy sponsors, so they drew huge crowds; famous gladiators became celebrities, as graffiti at Pompeii shows. They also had a political purpose: magistrates and candidates paid for games to win popularity and votes. The games also displayed Roman values such as courage and discipline in front of the whole community.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies a reason (e.g. free entertainment)
1 mark: explains it with evidence
1 mark: identifies a second reason (e.g. politics, Roman values)
1 mark: explains it with evidence

questions.solution: The games were free, exciting entertainment and a way for politicians to win support
questions.hint: Think about the crowd and about the people who paid for the games
